[2500012, 160] F8_E4M3 with one BF16 `weight_scale`: 320,001,536 rows of 160 values, 51.2 GB. The engine used to take
it from ISTA-DASLab's GGUF as IQ4_NL (90 B/row), which is 8% off these values per row; this keeps them bit for bit.

The output is a one-tensor GGUF: `per_layer_token_embd.weight`, ne = [160, 320001536], type I8 holding the FP8 bytes
(GGUF has no FP8 type), with `strata.ple.format` = "f8_e4m3" and `strata.ple.scale` (F32). The bytes are copied
straight out of the safetensors files in shard order - nothing is decoded or rounded - so memory stays flat.
"""
import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import struct
import sys

GGUF_TYPE_STRING, GGUF_TYPE_F32 = 8, 6
GGML_TYPE_I8 = 24
ALIGN = 32
CHUNK = 64 << 20


def safetensors_header(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        n = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]
        return json.loads(f.read(n)), 8 + n


def gguf_string(s):
    b = s.encode("utf-8")
    return struct.pack("<Q", len(b)) + b


def kv_string(key, val):
    return gguf_string(key) + struct.pack("<I", GGUF_TYPE_STRING) + gguf_string(val)


def kv_f32(key, val):
    return gguf_string(key) + struct.pack("<I", GGUF_TYPE_F32) + struct.pack("<f", val)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="the checkpoint directory (model.safetensors.index.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    model, out = pathlib.Path(a.model), pathlib.Path(a.out)
    wmap = json.loads((model / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["weight_map"]

    shards = {}
    scale_name = None
    for name in wmap:
        if ".ngram_embedding.shard_" in name and name.endswith(".weight"):
            shards[int(name.rsplit(".shard_", 1)[1].split(".")[0])] = name
        elif name.endswith(".ngram_embedding.weight_scale"):
            scale_name = name
    if not shards or scale_name is None:
        sys.exit("no ngram_embedding shards / weight_scale in " + str(model))
    if sorted(shards) != list(range(len(shards))):
        sys.exit("the n-gram shards are not numbered 0..%d without gaps" % (len(shards) - 1))

    hdr, base = safetensors_header(model / wmap[scale_name])
    t = hdr[scale_name]
    if t["dtype"] != "BF16" or t["shape"] not in ([1], []):
        sys.exit("unexpected weight_scale: %s %s" % (t["dtype"], t["shape"]))
    with open(model / wmap[scale_name], "rb") as f:
        f.seek(base + t["data_offsets"][0])
        (bits,) = struct.unpack("<H", f.read(2))
    scale = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", bits << 16))[0]

    parts, rows, dim = [], 0, None
    for k in range(len(shards)):
        name = shards[k]
        hdr, base = safetensors_header(model / wmap[name])
        t = hdr[name]
        if t["dtype"] != "F8_E4M3" or len(t["shape"]) != 2:
            sys.exit("%s is %s %s, not a 2-D F8_E4M3 tensor" % (name, t["dtype"], t["shape"]))
        if dim is None:
            dim = t["shape"][1]
        if t["shape"][1] != dim or t["data_offsets"][1] - t["data_offsets"][0] != t["shape"][0] * dim:
            sys.exit("%s: inconsistent shape %s" % (name, t["shape"]))
        parts.append((model / wmap[name], base + t["data_offsets"][0], t["shape"][0] * dim))
        rows += t["shape"][0]
    print("%d shards, %d rows x %d, scale %.9g, %.2f GB" % (len(parts), rows, dim, scale, rows * dim / 1e9), flush=True)

    kvs = [kv_string("general.architecture", "strata-ple"),
           kv_string("general.name", "PLE n-gram table, FP8 E4M3 as shipped"),
           kv_string("strata.ple.format", "f8_e4m3"),
           kv_f32("strata.ple.scale", scale),
           kv_string("strata.ple.source", model.name)]
    head = b"GGUF" + struct.pack("<IQQ", 3, 1, len(kvs)) + b"".join(kvs)
    head += gguf_string("per_layer_token_embd.weight") + struct.pack("<I", 2) + struct.pack("<QQ", dim, rows)
    head += struct.pack("<I", GGML_TYPE_I8) + struct.pack("<Q", 0)
    head += b"\0" * ((-len(head)) % ALIGN)

    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = out.with_suffix(out.suffix + ".part")
    written = 0
    with open(tmp, "wb") as w:
        w.write(head)
        for i, (path, off, n) in enumerate(parts):
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                f.seek(off)
                left = n
                while left:
                    b = f.read(min(CHUNK, left))
                    if not b:
                        sys.exit("short read in " + str(path))
                    w.write(b)
                    left -= len(b)

| `runtime.verify.plan` | `load` | Read the ready owner and instance IDs, model load state and whether this check would load the model. It performs no probe and creates no journal entry. |
| `runtime.verify` | `wait_s`, `load`, `if_owner_id`, `if_instance_id` | Recheck the reviewed owner and instance inside the owner host before checking API identity, launch attestation and generation when loaded. It may explicitly load a model and is journaled. Both IDs are required by the Desktop bridge; direct CLI verification may omit them. |
| `runtime.stop.plan` | none | Read the current owner ID and, when available, engine instance ID; no drain or journal entry. |
| `runtime.stop` | `wait_s`, `if_owner_id`, `if_instance_id` | Drain and stop only the reviewed owner and instance; journal the outcome. `if_owner_id` is required by the Desktop bridge. |

Desktop benchmark review bounds the total phase count and per-request timeout against its 1,900-second bridge deadline; longer workloads remain available through `strata bench run`. Saved-profile CLI runs and Desktop runs share a local per-profile benchmark lease that refuses overlapping launches; a raw `--url` run has no saved-profile lease. `STRATA_API_KEY` and optional `STRATA_TELEMETRY_KEY` are read only by the host process. Desktop now creates a private journal receipt before launch and recovers a job by ID after a host restart. The phase progress file and final report persist in the private output directory. Reports retain the planned and completed phase counts; success requires every planned phase to pass. A caught phase exception saves partial evidence and is labelled incomplete in the Desktop and Markdown export; an abrupt process kill can leave only the last progress record. Operator cancellation closes active benchmark-owned response streams and saves `cancelled: true`, `successful: false`, and a `cancelled` final progress state. It can take up to the configured request timeout if a connection has not received response headers yet. The request marker is an acknowledgement, not the final outcome. A malformed postflight telemetry response is saved as failed evidence with unavailable after-state. The exact-run lease check distinguishes a process still holding that path from one that released it. `other_active` and `untracked` do not prove that the saved run is alive. A held lease does not prove that inference is making progress. A crash before the benchmark creates an output directory can leave only the receipt; after the launch window it is labelled `completion_unknown`. Windows lease and receipt recovery still need target qualification.

Times are seconds. `if_profile_revision` is a 16-character lowercase profile revision; `if_source_sha256` is a 64-character lowercase digest. For start, take them from `runtime.start.plan` as `plan.launch.profile_revision` and `plan.source_sha256`. For restart, take `candidate_profile_revision`, `candidate_source_sha256`, `current_owner_id` and `current_instance_id` from `runtime.restart.plan`. For stop, take `plan.owner_id` and `plan.instance_id` from `runtime.stop.plan`; the instance ID may be `null` while the engine is starting or has failed. Owner and instance IDs are 32-character lowercase values when present. Restart plans require a ready instance, so both identities are present. The bridge rejects stale restart and stop reviews before journaling; the owner host checks again before draining. A stale start plan is rejected before the journal begins when possible; the owner host checks the same preconditions again immediately before launching the engine. A plan does not reserve the profile, source file or instance. An interrupted or timed-out mutating call may have an uncertain outcome. Inspect the operation journal and runtime status before retrying; never assume the process exit reversed a side effect.

## Desktop adapter requirements

The Desktop host now maps one configured profile's Start, Stop, Restart and Verify controls to these typed actions and displays the returned operation ID and owner state. A changed source config causes the first Restart review to refuse the action and show an explicit source-change review; the second plan sets only the operator-selected source-switch/migration allowances and displays the candidate path, digest and rollback requirement before drain. Its Components screen reads the same `doctor.inspect` report as the CLI; the optional live card probe runs only after the operator requests it.
